title: Juniper and the Drop
premise: Beatrix Halloran, a financial-crimes investigator who once testified against the Voss network and vanished into witness protection, discovers her safe house listed online with interior photos — proof someone inside the program sold her out. The listing's metadata traces to a laundering pipeline called 'the Drop,' which moves cartel money through shell charities into clean government contracts. Hunted by a meticulous assassin named Ilse and betrayed by the marshal who protected her, Beatrix must smuggle evidence past three governments' competing interests, aided by Juniper, a teenage hacker squatting in her old life. In the end, Beatrix trades her own anonymity for the truth: she testifies publicly, burns the Drop, and chooses an unhidden, ordinary life over survival in the shadows.
about_author: Casper Vane is the pen name of a former compliance analyst who spent a decade tracing money through offshore ledgers before turning to fiction. They write from a small coastal town, where they claim the best plot twists arrive with the morning fog.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Beatrix, under her assumed name Mara, scrolls real estate sites at 2 a.m. and finds her safe house for sale — with photos of her go-bag on the bed. POV Beatrix. Emotional beat: cold dread; the polished lie begins cracking.

chapters.title: Go-Bag Protocol
chapters.summary: She runs extraction protocol, but every dead-drop contact is stale or dead. Her handler, Marshal Reyes, doesn't answer. POV Beatrix. Emotional beat: isolation sharpening into resolve as she realizes the breach is internal.

chapters.title: Juniper
chapters.summary: A teenager catches Beatrix breaking into her own former apartment — Juniper, a squatter-hacker who recognized the house from the listing and came sniffing. POV alternates. Emotional beat: wary mutual recognition between two people living off-grid.

chapters.title: Metadata
chapters.summary: Juniper strips the listing's metadata: uploaded via a government contractor server tied to shell charity 'Meridian Light.' Beatrix recognizes the laundering pattern from her old case. POV Juniper. Emotional beat: thrill curdling into fear.

chapters.title: The Drop
chapters.summary: Beatrix explains the pipeline: dirty money enters through charities, exits as clean contract payments — 'the Drop.' Someone inside witness protection fed her address to the network. POV Beatrix. Emotional beat: grief for the life she traded away now weaponized against her.

chapters.title: Ilse
chapters.summary: Introduce the assassin: Ilse reviews Beatrix's file in a Vienna hotel, noting the investigator's habits like a lover would. POV Ilse. Emotional beat: unsettling calm; the hunter's patience established.

chapters.title: Reyes
chapters.summary: Reyes finally calls — but his questions are wrong, scripted. Beatrix feeds him false coordinates and hangs up shaking. POV Beatrix. Emotional beat: betrayal confirmed; trust becomes a liability.

chapters.title: Three Governments
chapters.summary: Juniper maps the interested parties: US prosecutors want the file quiet, an EU auditor wants it loud, and a foreign intelligence service wants the contractors intact. POV Juniper. Emotional beat: the scale of the machine versus two nobodies.

chapters.title: Safe House Two
chapters.summary: They hole up in a decommissioned coast guard station. Beatrix trains Juniper in counter-surveillance; Juniper teaches her the modern internet. POV both. Emotional beat: belonging taking root where neither expected it.

chapters.title: The Ledger Fragment
chapters.summary: Juniper recovers a partial ledger from Meridian Light's breached backups — enough to prove the Drop, not enough to survive court. POV Juniper. Emotional beat: hope that demands more risk.

chapters.title: First Contact
chapters.summary: Beatrix approaches EU auditor Lena Brandt in Rotterdam, trading a fragment for protection. Brandt warns: three governments means three ways to bury the truth. POV Beatrix. Emotional beat: cautious alliance, old cynicism tested.

chapters.title: Close Call
chapters.summary: Ilse nearly takes Beatrix at the ferry terminal; Juniper's improvised drone diversion saves her. POV Ilse then Beatrix. Emotional beat: terror and gratitude braided together; the stakes turn physical.

chapters.title: What Reyes Knows
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: five years ago, Beatrix's testimony, Reyes swearing he'd protect her — and the moment the program started leaking. POV Beatrix (past). Emotional beat: understanding how survival was always the product being sold.

chapters.title: The Full Ledger
chapters.summary: The complete ledger sits in a contractor data vault in Zurich. Getting it requires credentials only Reyes holds. POV Beatrix. Emotional beat: the bitter math of needing your betrayer.

chapters.title: Baiting the Marshal
chapters.summary: They leak a fake location to draw Reyes out; instead Ilse comes, and Reyes arrives to warn them — he was played too, a cutout for Director Hale of the contractor firm. POV Reyes. Emotional beat: reluctant redemption offered, not yet accepted.

chapters.title: Zurich
chapters.summary: Infiltration of the vault: Juniper spoofs access while Beatrix walks the corridors of the company that erased her. They get the ledger; alarms trip. POV Beatrix. Emotional beat: triumph immediately priced in pursuit.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: Foreign intelligence seizes their courier copy at the border; Brandt goes dark; Ilse closes in. Everything seems lost. POV Juniper. Emotional beat: despair — but Juniper kept a second copy no one knew about.

chapters.title: The Price
chapters.summary: To publish safely, Beatrix must surface publicly — ending anonymity forever. She records her testimony naming Hale, the Drop, and the leak. POV Beatrix. Emotional beat: acceptance; choosing justice over survival.

chapters.title: Convergence
chapters.summary: Climax at a Brussels press deadline: Ilse corners Beatrix on the rooftop across from the media office. Reyes intervenes, takes a wound; Juniper uploads the ledger live. POV all three. Emotional beat: the truth escaping faster than any bullet.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: Hale arrested; Meridian Light dissolved; Brandt reopens the audit publicly. Ilse vanishes, contract voided — a nod of professional respect left behind. POV Ilse. Emotional beat: ambiguous closure; some debts unpaid.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Beatrix testifies under her real name, cameras rolling, three governments forced to listen. Reyes, recovering, watches from the gallery. POV Beatrix. Emotional beat: vindication that costs everything and gives back selfhood.

chapters.title: Unlisted
chapters.summary: Months later: Beatrix and Juniper share a small apartment above a bookshop, no go-bag, door unlocked. A new listing appears online — a house for sale, ordinary photos, nobody inside. POV Beatrix. Emotional beat: belonging earned; the price paid in full.
